text:
Maya Patel: Q — how should we let customers configure rate limits for Private/VPC deployments? customers want to manage policies themselves, but we still need consistent telemetry + fallback.

Ryan Chen: Two primary modes we discussed: 1) customer-managed local policy (file/agent inside VPC) 2) control-plane managed (customer config pushed to their private control plane). each has tradeoffs.

Elena Gomez: enforcement location matters. if we enforce at the local edge (nginx/envoy) we can keep enforcement low-latency, but how do we surface errors/metrics back to Redwood?

Samir Rao: Local token-bucket in the edge proxy + periodic metrics export is simplest. use a small daemon to emit Prometheus metrics and an audit log. bursts handled with a separate burst bucket (short window) and a steady bucket.

Ryan Chen: Example customer policy we prototyped (YAML):
```yaml
policy_version: v1
org_id: org-123
rules:
  - id: default-token
    key: api_key
    limit_per_minute: 60000
    burst_capacity: 500
    routes:
      - /v1/generate
      - /v1/embeddings
    behavior_on_violation: reject
```
We'd validate schema locally or in control plane.

Elena Gomez: We should require a policy metadata block with signed `policy_id` + `seq` so we can detect stale policies. also add `audit.logging: true` toggle so customers can opt-in to sending logs to our telemetry endpoint (or to S3/forwarder).

Maya Patel: UX question — in Private with customer-managed control plane, should Console still show the effective policy? or only when their control plane is online?

Ryan Chen: Console can show last-known policy and a live status (connected / disconnected). when disconnected show "effective: local" and display local policy hash. also surface `x-rw-rate-limit-*` headers for customers to debug.

ops-bot: curl test from inside VPC: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -i https://private-gw.local/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> returns 429 with headers: `x-rw-limit: 60000`, `x-rw-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-reset: 167`

Samir Rao: Need to avoid split-brain: if both control plane and local agent try to enforce different limits, tie-breaker is policy `seq` + signature. local agent should reject any policy with older seq or invalid sig.

Elena Gomez: Telemetry names (prelim): `redwood_private_ratelimit_allowed_total{org_id,route}` and `redwood_private_ratelimit_throttled_total{org_id,route,reason}`. also expose a gauge `redwood_private_ratelimit_burst_remaining{org_id}`.

Ryan Chen: Implementation notes:
- Use leaky/token bucket for correctness.
- Support per-key and per-org rules. customers want both; per-key overrides per-org.
- Burst window: short-term bucket + long-term refill.
- Expose headers: `x-rw-limit`, `x-rw-remaining`, `x-rw-reset`, `x-rw-burst`.

Maya Patel: Security: policies must be signed by customer's KMS or Redwood when managed. for Private/VPC we must accept both. documented key rotation required.

infra-sre-bot: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/372-rate-limits-private (added) :white_check_mark:

Samir Rao: Edge corner case: very chatty clients can spin up many connections and evade per-connection token buckets. enforce at request-id / api-key granularity + connection limits at proxy.

Elena Gomez: Also add a safe default fallback: if no policy found, apply a conservative host-level limit (e.g., 100rps per-org) and alert customer. never default to unlimited.

Maya Patel: Action items: 1) Ryan to draft policy schema + header spec 2) Samir to prototype Envoy filter with dual-bucket 3) Elena to add telemetry names and audit log spec 4) I'll write Console display mockups. Deadline EOD Fri?

Ryan Chen: I'll start on schema PR. ping me with edge cases.

Samir Rao: I can spin up a PoC in dev VPC, will post numbers.

Elena Gomez: I'll add audit lines to the logs: `policy_id`, `policy_seq`, `enforced_by` (local|controlplane).

Maya Patel: Thanks — biggest remaining question: do we allow customers to fully opt-out of telemetry shipping? we can, but must then drop to degraded UX (no aggregated metrics in Console). thoughts?

Ryan Chen: allow opt-out but require local retention and on-demand export (legal/compliance). show warning in Console.

ops-bot: created issue #4127 for "private rate-limit config UX" in product board.

Maya Patel: cool. follow-ups next week after PRs land.
